message:
The device fits and survives storm push with ordinary margins. Plain words first: the spinning disc leaves a finger width per side and pushes like a heavy shopping bag on a scaffold pole. Side gap 2.50 cm in the side clearance (E74) clears deflection 0.516 mm in the post tip deflection (E26) and stack 36.0 cm in the axial stack length (E52) sits inside 45 cm, while thrust 37.3 N in the survival thrust (E22) with moment 13.1 N·m in the overturning moment (E23) gives stress 16.6 MPa in the bending stress (E27) against yield in the Aluminum 6061-T6 — Material Datasheet (E55), all ordinary body-weight and doorway scales.

It makes useful power across wind with touch-safe volts. Plain words first: the same blades spin the same speeds but the rewound generator wakes the regulator at light wind, rising from night-light to laptop level. Shaft 3.27 W in the shaft power at 5 m/s (E11) to regulated 22.1 W in the regulated load power (E66) at speeds 1.43e+03 to 3.15e+03 Revolutions Per Minute (RPM), meaning shaft turns per minute, in the rpm at 5 m/s (E14) and the rpm at 11 m/s (E13), with volts 8.41 to 18.5 V in the required Kv revision (E76) inside 8 to 40 V in the Buck/Boost Converter - 8-40V to 12V/3A | Little Bird Electronics (E60), where Kv means turns per volt; low regulated 2.08 W in the low-wind regulated power (E80) confirms light-wind feed.

It stops fast and stays stopped with bulb-level heat and no open block. Plain words first: the resistor plus spring grip stops the spin in under a second then holds like a hand grip beating a shopping-bag pull, with a brief household-bulb flash. Stop 0.673 s to threshold 315 RPM in the 10 percent threshold (E75) and 0 RPM at 10 s in the upgraded stop (E70) against the 10 s rule in the CWC 2019 Rules and Requirements Manual (E41), hold 0.80 N·m beating storm 0.48 N·m in the electrical-only runaway check (E48) and factored 0.72 N·m in the required hold torque (E54), dump 85.6 W in the revised dump power (E78) superseding 51.1 W in the dump resistor power (E39) with spin 109 J in the spin-down energy (E47) and rise 4.35 K in the brake disc temperature (E53). I accept the ready votes of Safety-Control Integrator and Aero-Rotor Lead and Structures-Survival Engineer and Power-Systems Engineer on v2, since both blocking objections are resolved and remaining power-curve and timed-stop and re-latch and parked-torque checks are named bench tests needing built hardware.

RECORD: Decided is 40 cm SD7080 fixed-pitch rotor with soft stall plus hub on stiff nacelle-post mount driving 170-180 Kv outrunner bridge to buck-boost plus dump grid with Normally Closed (NC), meaning wired shut until opened, chain sense to 0.80 N-m spring disc plus dump; numbers standing are clearance 2.50 cm (E74), stack 36.0 cm (E52), thrust 37.3 N (E22), stress 16.6 MPa (E27), power 3.27 W (E11) to 22.1 W (E66), volts 8.41 to 18.5 V (E76), stop 0.673 s to 0 RPM (E70), dump 85.6 W (E78); still open are only named bench tests for power curve plus timed stop plus re-latch restart and parked torque owed by Aero-Rotor Lead plus Power-Systems Engineer plus Safety-Control Integrator, with no blocking objection open. Ready, because no blocking objection is open and every member's opinion on current v2 is given and answered.
Note on Aero-Rotor Lead: Kept rotor speeds and powers through Kv fix and owes power-curve and parked-torque bench proof.
Note on Structures-Survival Engineer: Confirmed thrust and fit unchanged by Kv swap with clear margins.
Note on Power-Systems Engineer: Supplied Kv correction spanning regulation with dump as slowing aid.
Note on Safety-Control Integrator: Proved fast stop and parked hold with latched chain and owes timed-stop and re-latch tests.
